findings.reason: A square showing the adjacent-factor projection factoring through the closed incidence locus materially clarifies how independent Grassmannian choices become nested flags. The original formula states nesting but does not display this map-level relationship. This is an explanatory diagram addition, not a gap in the original proof.
findings.action: Appended final Remarks defining P, Q_i, I_i and all maps, with one commuting tikzcd square and boundary cases n=1,2.

correction: Appended a commutative square Fl(V) -> P over I_i -> Q_i with horizontal closed inclusions, adjacent-factor projections, and explicit interpretation of the intersection of inverse images.

diagram_math_checks.result: For n>=3 and 1<=i<=n-2, both factors Gr(i,V), Gr(i+1,V) occur in P. They parameterize subspaces of dimensions i and i+1, not quotient spaces, by local supplier def-grassmannian-subspaces and F1. I_i consists exactly of nested such pairs by F3.

j:Fl(V)->P is the closed inclusion of step 1.1; pi_i:P->Q_i is the product projection, regular by the cited product definition; iota_i:I_i->Q_i is the closed inclusion of F3. rho_i:Fl(V)->I_i is the restriction of pi_i to flags, with codomain valid because V_i is contained in V_(i+1); the incidence closed-subvariety structure gives the factorization.

For every flag V_bullet, both iota_i composed with rho_i and pi_i composed with j give (V_i,V_(i+1)); these are the same coordinate-selection regular map. Horizontal hooks mean closed inclusions. No pullback claim for a single square, quotient identification, fibre identification, or rank assertion is made.

diagram_math_checks.check: Full incidence intersection and boundary cases
diagram_math_checks.result: A tuple in P belongs to every pi_i inverse image of I_i exactly when every successive pair is nested, hence is a complete flag after adding fixed endpoints 0 and V; this is step 1.1. For n=2 no such i exists and P=Gr(1,V); for n=1 the empty product is the point in step 1.1.
